transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. It's very nice to meet you too. Um... well, they actually sent me here from work. I'm an EMT. I really hope I'm not in too much trouble, it was just... I think it was just a bit of a misunderstanding, really. 

I was at the station, and I was moving the airway bags around. I just put them into a pattern that I knew was right, you know? Just trying to be helpful and keep things organized. I guess I was also repeating the dispatch numbers out loud while I did it, just to keep it all straight in my head. But then my lieutenant came over and told me to stop and step away, and... well, I feel really bad about this part, because I always respect my officers, but I wouldn't step away. 

I just couldn't. It felt like the whole bay would go bad if I broke the sequence. I was just trying to keep everything safe and running right... does that make sense? I really didn't mean to be insubordinate or cause a problem.

When you felt that the bay would 'go bad' if you stopped, did you feel like you were following a specific rule or standard of perfection, or did you feel like something terrible would actually happen to you or others if you didn't finish the pattern?

Oh, um... I'm not really sure. I definitely didn't think anything terrible was going to happen to anyone—I promise, I would never let anyone get hurt. I take my job really seriously, so I don't want you to think I was putting people in danger or anything like that. 

And it wasn't really like I was trying to be a perfectionist or follow a specific rule from the handbook, either. I just... I don't really know how to describe it better than that. It just felt like the bay would go bad if I didn't finish it. I didn't have a specific bad thing in mind, it was just this... this strong feeling that things wouldn't be right. 

I'm sorry, I know that's probably not a very helpful answer. I really don't want to sound like I'm making things difficult. I hope I'm explaining it okay... am I making any sense at all?

When you have these strong urges to arrange things in a pattern, do you feel like you are fighting against an unwanted impulse that you wish you could stop, or does it feel more like you are simply following your own internal standard for how things ought to be?

Um... I don't think it's really either of those, to be honest. I really hope it's okay to say that. 

I definitely don't feel like I'm fighting against it, like it's some bad impulse I want to stop. I mean, I'm just trying to help out and do my job well, you know? But... it's not really about my own personal standard for how things ought to be, either, like I'm just being picky about a messy room. It's just... the pattern was what the bags needed to be in that moment. I didn't feel like I was fighting anything at all. 

I'm sorry, I know you gave me two choices and I didn't really pick either one. I'm really trying to answer correctly for you. Does that help at all, or should I try to explain it differently?
When you felt the bags needed to be in that specific pattern, did you believe that you had a special understanding or insight into the situation that the other EMTs at the station did not have?

Oh, um, no... definitely not. I really don't think I have any kind of special understanding or... or insight, like you said. 

I mean, the other guys at the station are all really great medics and EMTs, and I respect them a lot. I would never want to act like I'm smarter or know more than they do, I promise. It wasn't about me being special or having some secret knowledge. It was just... I just saw the bags and that's just how they had to go right then. 

I really hope I don't sound arrogant or like I think I'm better than anyone else, because I definitely don't. I'm just a regular guy trying to do my part for the shift. Does that make sense? I really hope I'm answering your questions the right way.

When you are in the middle of arranging those bags and you feel the need to complete the pattern, do you feel a sense of internal tension, anxiety, or discomfort that only goes away once you finish, or is it just a neutral sense of 'this is how it should be'?

Um... I guess it's more neutral? I don't really feel anxious or... or tense about it. I definitely don't want you to think I'm having panic attacks or getting all worked up over some bags, you know? 

It's really just... I start doing it, and it just feels like the right thing to do to finish it. It's not like this big uncomfortable feeling that I'm trying to get rid of. I just sort of... do it. 

I hope that's the kind of answer you're looking for. I know sometimes these things can sound a little weird, but I promise I'm not, like, losing my mind over it or anything. I'm just trying to keep the bay organized. Is that... is that okay? I'm not making it sound worse than it is, am I?
When you were repeating the dispatch numbers out loud, did you feel like you were hearing them from somewhere else, or that someone or something was prompting you to say them?

Um... no. No, definitely not. I didn't hear them from anywhere else, and there wasn't anyone or anything prompting me to say them. 

I really hope it didn't come across like I was hearing voices or something. I know that would be a really bad thing, especially in my line of work, and I promise I'm not experiencing anything like that. I think I was just... you know, just saying the numbers out loud to make sure I had them right in my head? Just trying to be thorough so I don't mess up a call or let my partner down. 

I really want to make sure I'm doing a good job, you know? I hope that makes sense. I'm not giving you any reason to be concerned about me hearing things, am I? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it right so you don't worry.
When you say the bags 'had to' be in that pattern, do you feel like that arrangement has a specific, hidden meaning or significance that others just aren't seeing?

Um... no, not at all. I don't think there's any kind of hidden meaning or... or secret message in how they're set up. I really don't. 

I definitely don't want you to think I'm reading into things that aren't there, or... or acting strange about it. I know how important it is to just stick to the facts on the job. It's really just about keeping the equipment tidy, you know? Just making sure everything is where it belongs so we're ready for the next call. 

I'm just trying to be a good team player and keep the station looking professional. There's no weird significance to it, I promise. I hope that's okay? I really don't want you to think I'm seeing things that aren't there. I'm doing okay, right?

In general, outside of these specific moments at work, would you say that you are someone who is often described as very rigid, preoccupied with rules, or overly focused on lists and organization to the point where it sometimes makes it hard to finish your tasks?

Um... no, I wouldn't say that. I don't think I'm overly rigid or anything like that. I mean, I like things to be organized, sure, but... but not to the point where it gets in the way of my work. 

I definitely don't want you to think I'm some kind of control freak or that I can't get my job done because I'm obsessing over lists. In EMS, you have to be flexible, you know? Things change fast, and I pride myself on being able to roll with it. 

I just try to do my job well and keep things in order when I have the downtime. It's just normal organization, really. I'm not... I'm not too focused on it, I promise. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not giving you the wrong impression about how I work. I really try to just be easygoing and get things done.

When you are in that moment of arranging the bags, does it feel like you are following a 'just right' feeling—where the action feels inherently correct or satisfying in a way that is hard to put into words—even though you don't feel anxious or tense?

Um... no, I wouldn't say it's like that. It's not... it's not a special 'just right' feeling or anything hard to explain like that. 

I just... I just put them where they're supposed to go. It's really just about being practical, you know? Like, anyone would put them there so they're easy to grab in an emergency. 

I really hope it doesn't sound like I'm doing things for weird reasons. I definitely don't get some kind of... strange satisfaction from it or anything. I just want to be a good EMT and keep the rig ready for my partner. 

I'm not doing anything wrong by keeping them neat, am I? I just want to make sure I'm answering this right so you know I'm totally focused on the actual work. I'm doing exactly what I'm supposed to be doing, right?

Have you ever felt that there is a specific, underlying order to the world or the way things are arranged that you are somehow uniquely responsible for maintaining, even if you don't think it has a 'hidden' meaning?

Um, no... no, definitely not. I don't feel like I'm responsible for, you know, the whole world or anything big like that. I'm just an EMT. I just focus on my rig and my gear. 

I wouldn't want you to think I've got some sort of... grand idea about myself or that I think I'm special in that way. I just like to do my part, you know? Keep my little corner of things neat so I don't let my partner down. 

I'm really just trying to be a reliable guy. There's no... I don't have any strange ideas about the universe or anything. I'm just doing my job the best I can. That's normal, isn't it? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right idea here. I'm not sounding crazy or anything, am I?
